title: The Perfect Verdict
premise: Estate lawyer Ines Nystrom, the quiet archivist of Grayhollow's secrets, is reading the will of matriarch Vera Lindqvist when a confession letter arrives—postmarked the day after Vera's funeral, written in a hand that died ten years ago. The letter points to a second will, hidden inside the town's own records, and to the truth behind the drowning everyone agreed to forget. As Ines follows the paper trail, she realizes the killer is someone who has been watching her file the town's secrets for a decade—and who now needs her silence. In the end, Ines chooses exposure over invisibility, reading the true will aloud at a public hearing and trapping the killer with a forged filing date only the murderer could have corrected.
about_author: N. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent years handling probate files and the secrets they contain. They write mysteries about ordinary people whose meticulous lives conceal extraordinary courage.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ines Nystrom, POV. Ten days after Vera Lindqvist's funeral, Ines reads a will dated after the one she notarized herself. The emotional beat is unease: her ordered world develops its first crack, and she realizes someone used her own filing system against her.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. A confession letter arrives, postmarked the day after the funeral, written in the hand of Daniel Voss—who drowned ten years ago. She recognizes the paper stock from her own office supplies. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve: someone is staging a resurrection.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, with flashbacks to her first year in Grayhollow. She audits her decade of files and finds three pages razored out of the Voss case folder. The beat is grief: the archive she built as armor was also a weapon waiting to be turned.

chapters.title: The Heirs
chapters.summary: Ines interviews Vera's heirs: son Marcus, estranged daughter Liv, and caretaker Ruth. Each lies differently about the night Daniel died. The beat is suspicion layered over loneliness, as Ines realizes these near-strangers know more about her than she does.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, joined by deputy Amara Okafor, the one investigator who never closed the Voss case. They pull the coroner's original report: blunt force before the drowning. The beat is alliance—the first belonging Ines has felt in years, and it makes her a target.

chapters.title: A Correction in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. The killer mails her a 'corrected' copy of the false will, fixing an error only the forger would catch—a trap meant to frame her. The beat is terror curdling into clarity: the killer isn't hiding from her; they're teaching her.

chapters.title: The Second Filing
chapters.summary: Ines and Amara trace a sealed amendment filed under a dead clerk's credentials. Inside: Vera's real will disinheriting Marcus and funding an inquiry into Daniel's death. The beat is vindication shadowed by danger—Vera knew, and died arranging the reveal.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The caretaker confesses she saw Marcus strike Daniel but was paid to forget—by Vera, to protect the family name. The beat is complicity and sorrow: everyone Ines trusted kept the same file, just shelved differently.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. At the public probate hearing, Ines reads the true will aloud while Amara watches Marcus, who came to contest it. When Marcus corrects the filing date aloud—an error no innocent man could spot—Amara arrests him. The beat is triumph earned through exposure.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, weeks later. She reopens her archive, adds the truth to the record, and accepts Liv's invitation to Sunday dinner—the found family she never filed away. The final beat is quiet peace: invisible no longer, and glad of it.
